old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-jkuj","title":"Python slot claim: claim_seq not upper-bounded at decode/construct — accepts \u003eu32::MAX that Rust rejects (interop divergence)","description":"Codereview finding (l1qw.20.5 edge pass, verified live with cbor2): python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py:251-253 (decode_cose) and :176-178 (__post_init__) check only 'type(claim_seq) is not int or claim_seq \u003c 0'. cbor2 decodes major-type-0 uint 2**32 and tag-2 bignums to Python int, passing the guard. Rust bounds the same wire field: rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs:590 u32::try_from(seq) -\u003e MalformedClaim; bignums fail p.uint() outright. A validly-signed wire claim with claim_seq = 2**32 is fully accepted and cached by Python but rejected by Rust — cross-implementation verdict divergence on identical wire input. Now that claim_seq is the operative replay-gate value (l1qw.20.4 Rust / l1qw.20.5 Python), the divergence directly affects replay-state parity. Sender mirror trap: encode_claim_canonical (:310) emits unbounded claim_seq, so a Python gateway whose counter exceeds u32::MAX mints claims every Rust receiver drops as malformed. Fix: reject claim_seq \u003e 0xFFFFFFFF in both __post_init__ and decode_cose; pin with a boundary test (2**32-1 accepted, 2**32 rejected) and a wire-level decode test.
